chapter.name: Elections
chapter.blurb: Why elections matter, electoral systems, election laws and delimitation, the Election Commission, political parties and defection, and challenges to free and fair elections.

concepts.name: Why elections matter: direct and indirect elections
concepts.description: The importance of regular elections, direct and indirect elections in India and the meaning of psephology.
concepts.idea: Regular elections let citizens choose and hold accountable those who make decisions on their behalf.
concepts.rule: Members of the Lok Sabha, Vidhan Sabha and local bodies are directly elected every five years. The President, Vice President and members of the Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected. Psephology is the scientific study of elections (Greek psephos, pebble).
concepts.example: A class representative cannot continue for ever without a fresh election, and a government cannot continue beyond its term without a mandate.

concepts.name: Electoral systems: FPTP and proportional representation
concepts.description: The First-Past-The-Post system, proportional representation with single transferable vote, and the bicameral structure of legislatures in six states.
concepts.idea: An electoral system decides how votes are converted into seats.
concepts.rule: India chose the plurality (First-Past-The-Post) system for the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha. The Rajya Sabha, President, Vice President and Vidhan Parishad use proportional representation by the single transferable vote. Six states have a bicameral legislature with a Vidhan Parishad and a Vidhan Sabha.
concepts.example: Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh have two houses.

concepts.name: Election laws and delimitation of constituencies
concepts.description: The Representation of the People Acts, electoral offences and corrupt practices, and the delimitation of constituencies.
concepts.idea: Laws and delimitation make elections fair, transparent and equal in representation.
concepts.rule: RPA 1950: allocation of seats, delimitation, electoral rolls and the right of every citizen of 18 or above to vote. RPA 1951: nominations, campaigns, voting, disputes, electoral offences and corrupt practices. Delimitation fixes constituency boundaries under Article 82; there have been four Commissions (1952, 1963, 1973, 2002).

concepts.name: The Election Commission of India and its functions
concepts.description: The constitutional status of the ECI, its officers, its functions such as electoral rolls, scheduling, registering parties and symbols, and inclusive voting initiatives.
concepts.idea: The ECI is an autonomous constitutional body that supervises, directs and controls the whole election process.
concepts.rule: ECI: autonomous permanent constitutional body established on 25 January 1950 (Articles 324-329). Functions: prepare electoral rolls and conduct Special Intensive Revision, decide election schedule, register parties and allot symbols, ensure free and fair elections. Initiatives: voting from home, ETPBS, cVIGIL.
concepts.example: In 2024 voting from home was extended across India for senior citizens above 85 and persons with 40 per cent benchmark disability.

concepts.name: Political parties, defection and alliances
concepts.description: The role of political parties in elections, the multi-party system, the Anti-Defection Law, recognition of parties and coalitions.
concepts.idea: Political parties present programmes and policies, and the law prevents members from switching sides for personal gain.
concepts.rule: India has a multi-party system. Defection is switching from the party under whose banner one was elected. The Anti-Defection Law (1985, 52nd Amendment) can disqualify a member who voluntarily gives up party membership or votes against the whip. Alliances began in 1967; the Janata Party formed the first coalition government at the Centre in 1977.
concepts.example: Since the late 1990s the NDA and the UPA have been the major alliances.

concepts.name: Challenges to free and fair elections and the importance of voting
concepts.description: Challenges such as misinformation and intimidation, the safeguards of the Model Code of Conduct, EVMs and VVPAT, and why voting matters.
concepts.idea: Free and fair elections face practical challenges that the law, the ECI and active citizens work to overcome.
concepts.rule: Challenges include misinformation, fake news and intimidation. The ECI responds through RPA 1950 and 1951, the Model Code of Conduct, EVMs, VVPAT, voter awareness campaigns and technology. Casting a vote is a constitutional right as well as a duty; elections are the soul of democracy.
